content: Credentialing is the administrative process used to verify the qualifications of licensed professionals, organizational members, or organizations. This process involves assessing their background and legitimacy to ensure they meet the required standards. Many healthcare institutions and provider networks perform their own credentialing procedures. These are typically carried out by a credentialing specialist or through an electronic service. The results are then reviewed by a medical staff or credentialing committee to ensure compliance with institutional standards. Credentialing may include the granting and periodic review of specific clinical privileges. It also encompasses membership in medical or allied health staff, ensuring that individuals are qualified to perform their designated roles. The credentialing process is generally an objective evaluation of an individual’s current licensure, training, experience, competence, and ability to deliver specific services or perform particular procedures. This ensures that the professional is capable of meeting the demands of their role safely and effectively. Personnel credentialing is typically conducted at the start of employment, during the initial application process, and is repeated at regular intervals thereafter, known as reappointment. This ensures ongoing compliance with professional and institutional standards. Credentialing of vendors or other organizations often begins before the purchasing process and is repeated regularly to maintain quality and legitimacy in business relationships. In the political context, political parties credential their delegates during conventions to verify their eligibility and authority to participate in decision-making processes.
